findings.affected_surface: go_exported_api: Exported Go methods on *CrossOriginProtection in net/http standard library
findings.old_behavior: AddTrustedOrigin accepted origins containing userinfo (e.g. https://@example.com, https://foo:bar@example.com) as valid, since the validation only checked for path, query, and fragment. The error message for rejected origins was: "invalid origin %q: path, query, and fragment are not allowed".
findings.new_behavior: AddTrustedOrigin now rejects origins containing userinfo (when u.User != nil). The validation also checks u.User in addition to path, query, and fragment. The error message for rejected origins is now: "invalid origin %q: userinfo, path, query, and fragment are not allowed".
findings.compatibility_reason: Callers that previously passed origins containing userinfo (empty or non-empty) to AddTrustedOrigin would receive nil error (success), but after this change they will receive a non-nil error and the origin will not be registered as trusted. This represents a tightening of the input contract — previously valid inputs are now rejected. Additionally, the error message text has changed for all rejected origins (now includes "userinfo" in the list), which could affect any code that performs string matching on error messages from this function.
findings.why_not_internal_only: AddTrustedOrigin is an exported method on the exported type CrossOriginProtection in the Go standard library's net/http package. It is part of the public Go compatibility guarantee and can be called by any downstream Go program.
findings.uncertainty: The practical impact is limited because the Go stdlib documentation for AddTrustedOrigin states that Origin header values are of the form "scheme://host[:port]", which per the HTTP spec does not include userinfo. Callers passing userinfo-containing origins were already violating the documented contract. However, the method previously accepted these inputs, and any existing code relying on that acceptance would break.
findings.recommended_review: No manual review required. The change is intentional and correctly aligns the implementation with the documented API contract and HTTP specification.
findings.test_recommendation: Test AddTrustedOrigin with origins containing userinfo (both empty like https://@example.com and non-empty like https://foo:bar@example.com) to verify they are now properly rejected. Verify that origins without userinfo continue to be accepted. Verify the error message format for backward-compatibility with any error-message-dependent logic (though string matching on error messages is not idiomatic Go).
